title: Global Verdier duality
statement:
Fix primes $p$ and $\ell$ with $\ell\ne p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements, and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] on finite-type $k$-schemes at these coefficient stages, with its axioms (A1)--(A6) and their specified constructible finite-Tor domains. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and fix $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. Let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite
type and geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of pure dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension] over $k$, with
structure morphism $a_X$. Use the constructible exceptional inverse image
$Ra_X^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], at the coefficient stage
specified above. At every finite stage $A_{E,m}$, $m\geq1$, the structure
morphism is exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility], with cohomological and Tor bounds independent of
$m$, since it is separated of finite type. At integral and field stages
use the integral, rationalized, and common-stage exceptional functors in
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the adjunctions specified by the
fixed datum [def-sf-datum]. No additional admissibility hypothesis is imposed. Assume either
that $X$ is proper, or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated
finite-type, geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; in the latter
case no properness is required. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Then
there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma\bigl(X,\mathbb D_XK\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], natural in $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$
and compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and shifts. For
$K=\Lambda_X$ it specializes to
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$.

Here $\mathbb D_XK$ and $\omega_X$ have the meanings of [def-sf-pf], and
$R\Gamma_c,R\Gamma$ are the coefficient complexes of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The displayed isomorphism is first
an isomorphism in the coefficient-complex target of $\operatorname{Fib}_s$
of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$,
$D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$, or the stagewise
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, according to $\Lambda$.
Its formulation in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ means its transport through the
inverse of that equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]. The superscript $\vee$ in the coefficient
category means $R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$, at a common finite
field stage for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Finite-reduction compatibility
is asserted at finite and integral coefficients, and rationalization and
scalar-extension compatibility at the field stages where those operations
are defined, as in axiom (A5) of [def-sf-datum].

proof.text: Specialize the existing Verdier exchange theorem to a_X:X→Spec k. Apply lem-sf-global-identity-normalization to obtain normalized closed structures and the evaluation-transposed epsilon as a natural transformation with signed shifts and coefficient equations, but no inverse.

For each K and test object T, compose the inverse point tensor-Hom bijection, precomposition by the projection isomorphism, exceptional adjunction, the identity dualizing comparison, tensor-Hom on X and pull/star adjunction. Projection naturality and adjunction naturality prove naturality in T. Apply isoOfNaturalHomEquiv to the resulting Hom bijections. Expansion at the identity shows that its hom is exactly StageData.epsilon. Thus every epsilon component is invertible. Promote the recorded transformation to StageConclusion, retaining exactly its shifts.

For the tensor-Hom adjunction at the tensor unit, compare its right adjoint with the identity using Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq and the right-unitor adjunction. The counit equation gives exactly inverse right unitor followed by evaluation; the reverse comparison is exactly the transpose of the right unitor. These comparisons are inverse. Compose this unit isomorphism with the same epsilon component, then assemble Package from the normalized ring, projection, unit, signed-shift and coefficient records.

proof_origin.place: T2 Lean reduction: identity normalization, explicit Yoneda invertibility via the five adjunction bijections, and tensor-unit evaluation identities.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], assume that $k$ is separably closed, and
let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite
type and geometrically connected of pure dimension $d$ over $k$, with
structure morphism $a_X$ (no admissibility hypothesis: $Ra_X^!$ is the
constructible exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $a_X$ is exceptionally admissible
in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility] as every separated finite-type
morphism is). Assume either
that $X$ is proper, or that $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated
finite-type, geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; in the latter
case no properness is required. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$. Then
there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\Gamma\bigl(X,\mathbb D_XK\bigr)
$$

in the point category $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ of
[def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], natural in $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$
and compatible with shifts. For
$K=\Lambda_X$ it specializes to
$R\Gamma_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong R\Gamma(X,\omega_X)$.

proof.text:
Apply [thm-sf-verdier-exchange] with $Y=s$, $f=a_X$ and $M=K$:
$D_s(Ra_{X!}K)\cong Ra_{X*}D_XK$. Apply $\Fib_s$ and the point
identifications of [lem-sf-point], which apply since $k$ is separably
closed: the left-hand side becomes
$R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda)=R\Gamma_c(X,K)^\vee$
and the right-hand side becomes
$\Fib_s(Ra_{X*}D_XK)=R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$. Since $\Fib_s$ is an
equivalence onto the point category by [lem-sf-point], the resulting
composite is an isomorphism in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, and it is the displayed
isomorphism; naturality and the compatibility with shifts are those of
the two ingredients. The argument uses only the exceptional adjunction for $a_X$ (so that
[thm-sf-verdier-exchange] applies to $f=a_X$, $Y=s$), which is available
for every separated finite-type morphism, never that $a_X$ is proper: the compact-support image
$Ra_{X!}$ and the ordinary image $Ra_{X*}$ enter as two different
functors, and no comparison $Ra_{X!}\cong Ra_{X*}$ is invoked. Hence the
same proof covers both cases of the hypothesis, the proper one and the
nonproper one $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. The constant case is
$\mathbb D_X\Lambda_X=R\mathcal H om_X(\Lambda_X,Ra_X^!\Lambda)=\omega_X$
by [def-sf-pf].
